H.answer: No, the Supreme Court in Minor v. Happersett (ID: 88_0162-01) did not hold that the Fourteenth Amendment automatically guarantees women the right to vote in state presidential elections. The Court held that the provisions of the Constitution and laws of the State of Missouri, which confined the right of suffrage and registration to men, were not necessarily in violation of the Constitution of the United States. The Court stated that the question of whether a woman, as a citizen of the United States and of the State of Missouri, was a voter in that State, was not necessarily decided by the adoption of the Fourteenth Amendment.
